What I love about Canada is how diverse it is, so I'll break it down by cities I've spent time in:

Ottawa: Beautiful city. Has a small town feel but all the amenities of a large one. Ottawa had a reputation for being boring but I think a lot of that has changed recently. There are plenty of festivals and other touristy activities, pretty standard nightlife for Canada, and you're not far from a lot of other great locations. Weather wise, Ottawa is very season-centric and follows the typical Canada weather pattern of deathly hot during the summer and -20 in the winter. People wise, I find they are some what more mean and rude than a lot of their Canadian counter parts, not as bad as Toronto, but definitely a change if you're moving from BC or Quebec.

Montreal: In terms of culture and things to do, Montreal can't be beat. There is not shortage of things to do, and a lot of it is free or dirt cheap, and this is on top of being one of the cheapest cities to live in. It's also the largest city in Canada yet it feels a lot safer than a lot of other cities. When it comes to employment though, if you do not have a high level of bilingualism, you are out of luck. There are some anglophone centric jobs, but they are few and far between. People wise, 90% of the time it is amazing. At Tam Tams, you can go up to random people and start a conversation, and this holds true for Montreal in general. It's only that small minority of people that still hate anglos, and you won't encounter many of these people unless you go outside of the core. Weather wise, it's really just a slightly more cold winter than Ottawa.

Victoria: You've heard it a million times, no words can describe the beauty of British Colum...blah blah blah, yet it's pretty accurate. Vancouver Island is one of the few places you can go Kayaking and Snow Boarding in the same day. Very small city though, some people might find the culture lacking, as it's primarily a university and retirement town. People wise, people here are very nice. I remember everyone thanking the bus driver on daily basis when departing, people smile and will even converse with you randomly on the street. Everyone seems environmentally conscious, even some of the rural and red neck populations, Vancouver Island is the only place I've seen a NDP bumper sticker next to a Confederate flag sticker. Weather wise, probably the best in Canada, warm most of the year, decent amount of wind and rain for those uninitiated, practically no snow ever.

Toronto: I personally hated it here, ugly city with insane traffic. Very much felt like an american city in Canada. People were very rude, especially to minorities, I've watched people on multiple occasions treat service staff very badly. There's a lot to do here, and doesn't lack in culture, but only if you can afford to live here. Honestly, the class divide is also very apparent, I found just being here depressing and not an accurate portrayal of Canada. Weather wise, it's a lot better than Ottawa and Montreal, milder winters that end sooner.

[WP]On an expedition into the past, a time traveler is caught using a piece of future technology by a local

I never liked handling tourists, but it's easy money. Walk 'em around, make sure they don't freak out the locals, get 'em home without too much damage. It gets a bit monotonous after long enough. But at any job, given enough time, someone goes and fucks everything up.

It was a few years ago, details are a little fuzzy these days. We were in 19th century New England, posing as a group of traders going to the coast. Good way to see the scenery and talk to the locals. Tourists love it.

We were headed through the first town on the route. Before we warp, we've got a currency exchange where you can buy "Olde Tyme" money to buy things on the trip at about a 5:1 ratio. Inflation makes it way more profitable than it sounds. Anyway, we were in a general store, people were spending their money on jerky and other crap. Then a middle aged woman, I'd say about 45, whips out her fucking phone and takes a picture.

Now, most of the time we take people's stuff when they get into their clothes for the proper era. It prevents stuff like this from happening. However this woman had came in really convincing period clothes, so we let her wear it on the trip without checking her. You assume, "Hey, she knows enough about the time period that she can get a spot-on outfit, maybe she'll have the sense to not use a device that almost seems magic today in witch-burning New England." Apparently not.

So that goes about as well as you'd expect it to. The shopkeep sees the bright flash and hears the pseudo shutter sound, points and yells "Witch!" The locals approached her with caution, and I think performed a citizen's arrest. Although it looked a lot more like tackling her to the ground. My tourists got the hell out of there in all the commotion, and regrouped at our little wagon. I watched helplessly as the woman was dragged out of the store.

Now I know it sounds like she was pretty fucked. People accused of being witches didn't exactly get fair trails. But I had been in stickier situations. I had the other tourists go to the inn we were staying at that night, got them checked in and let them know we'd have to go back sooner than expected.

When the sun went down I made my move. One thing I love about the past is just how easy it is to move around at night. I already knew where the jailhouse was, as I'd been through this town more than once before. I approached from the south, as you could see someone approaching from any other direction. Crouching below the windows, I worked my way around to the front of the building.

I looked in through the window. The person guarding the front door was fast asleep in his chair. That definitely made the rest of this easier. I pushed open the door, slowly as to not make any noise. Through the crack, I looked down the barrel of a gun. That guy wasn't as asleep as he looked. "There's no reason to be sneaking around here. Reveal your hands to me and tell me exactly what your business is!" He said through the door.

I pulled the door shut, holding the handle tight in my hand. I felt the man pulling on the door, trying to pry it open. "What is going on? Open this door right now!" He shouted. I happily obliged, tackling the door in, and him to the ground. I kicked his gun away before he could lunge for it and stuffed a rag in his mouth before he could yell for help. I cuffed him with his own cuffs to a support beam in the room.

I looked at him before moving on and said "Sorry, man. Help will be here soon." Walking through the other doorway in the room I found myself among the cells, the furthest of which contained the tourist I was after.

The woman looked at me, her eyes red and cheeks puffy. She asked for help in a hoarse voice, and I responded by just putting my finger to my lips. The cell keys were hanging nearby on the wall. I grabbed them and unlocked her cell, letting her out. As we walked out of the jail, I picked up the jailer's revolver. He let out muffled cries in protest, but I just kept walking. Once outside I shot two rounds into the sky to bring people to help him out.

It didn't take long to get back to the inn. Didn't have much issue after that. People were obviously upset they only got to see one town before having to come back, had to give 'em refunds. And that one woman got a hell of a story to tell. But yeah, that's why I don't do the old New England run anymore.

Not so much a confined event as other things in this thread, but when I was in middle school and under a lot of stress from my mother's recent cancer diagnosis, I started to have weird feelings around trees. I would feel like I was being pulled towards them, like it was uncomfortable to move away and more comfortable to move towards them, and if I touched them, I would feel the way I do now if I touch someone I love a lot, but even stronger. I would feel like I melted into the tree and I would go into a kind of trance. My breathing and heart rate would slow way down and I always felt like if I hadn't kept a grip on myself I could have slipped away and died. It didn't scare me, though. It would just be merging with the world.

Around this same time, I discovered that I could do something that felt like flexing a muscle that would send a buzzing through my body. I felt like it streamed out of my fingers and toes if I wasn't touching anything, and moved into what I was touching otherwise.

These feelings are much reduced now, but I still feel peaceful and connected to the world when I'm outside, and I can still do the thing where I "exude energy" or whatever the heck it is. It doesn't seem to be related to any muscle, but it does result in an increased heart rate, faster the harder I "push". I looked on the internet, and there are a few people who can do this heart rate speeding up thing, and just like me, they feel like they can direct it to certain parts of their body, with different effects (e.g. give themselves a headache if they direct it at their head). Compositor here; worked on a few movies, Mad Max being one of them. There are a lot of factors in modern movies that take into account why the Visual Effects(vfx for short or CGI who don't know what it is) look bad and while there are a few videos out there on you-tube saying that older movies only had to match to a real environment and new movies are generating their environments without any real life footage, this is only a small problem mixed in with a whole lot of other problems.

These problems can be Directors and DOPs who don't understand how vfx work and are stuck in the old ways of filming they waste a lot of money in the filming process and editing process because they hadn't planned properly for the vfx and we end up with the phrase "oh we can just fix it in post" which courses more problems. Then theres the whole time it takes to make a film, back when all these old film were getting made there wasn't a quick turn around, they spent a few years making them. Now they give like a 2 year turn around to do everything. theres also another issue in the quick turn around for the vfx guys, its that we usually get the least amount of time to work on the film. The finally problem ill go over is that because you can pick and choose how you want things to look in vfx if the director doesn't have a clear vision on how things work in real life and how they look in their head we end up making multiple versions of things

There are a few more problems to go over but these are the major ones. if given time and the right director, you can get a full vfx (CGI) film with very little live action and it could look good we've just got to wait for the change
